description:
Record the customer's approval of a `PROPOSED` mapping. The mapping
carries an `APPROVE_MAPPING` confirmation in `pending_confirmations`, and
answering it here with the `approve` option is what unlocks
`prepress_submit_mapping`.

`confirmation_id` and `option_id` must both be copied verbatim from the
confirmation — `option_id` is the listed option, never a phrase the
customer typed and never a value you compose. If the customer does not
want this mapping, do not answer the confirmation: call
`prepress_map_pages` with the `positions` they ask for, or ask for
corrected files.

Returns a `job_id`. The result is the same shape as `prepress_map_pages`.
Job errors: `ConfirmationNotFoundError` (already answered, or wrong id),
`InvalidAnswerError` (option not on that confirmation), `AlreadyMappedError`
(this item already went through the one-way door), or `ItemHasDesignError`
(the item holds an attached design, which is what prints).
name: prepress_confirm

anyOf.description:
The Runner's response to a `@runner.job` invocation.

On the fast path (work completed within budget), `status` is SUCCEEDED
or FAILED and `result` / `error` is populated. On the slow path,
`status` is RUNNING and `job_id` is the handle the host LLM uses for
`poll()`.

On FAILED, `error` is the safe class-name code; `reason` / `detail` are
populated only when the failure carries a host-safe explanation (e.g. a
RendReal rejection's server message + body), else they stay None.

On RUNNING, `note` carries model-facing guidance: it tells the host LLM whether
a widget is already polling the job, or whether it must call `poll_job` itself.

Canonical short-circuit response shape.

`status` is always `"error"` — acts as a discriminator for LLM consumers.
`error` is a machine-readable code (e.g. `session_not_found`).
`reason` is a human-readable explanation of why the call failed.
`detail` carries structured extra context (ids, available values, etc.).

title: Record the mapping answer
